note: The alate is unknown; the original also describes a caste termed Pseudo-worker. The species name honours the collector Tarun K. Pal.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier has a body length of 8.40 mm; head with mandibles 3.20 mm, to the mandible base 2.25 mm; head width 1.48 mm, head height 1.23 mm; head index (width / length to the mandible base) 0.657. The left mandible has 4 marginal teeth and the right 2 (the descriptive text of the original records 3 marginal teeth on the left mandible and 2 on the right, and figure 9 shows 3 on the left and 2 on the right). Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 ring-like and the shortest. Postmentum constriction index 0.42, waist width 0.23 mm, less than half of the maximum width (0.55 mm). Pronotum 0.83 mm long and 1.40 mm wide. The pseudo-worker has a body length of 6.3—7.5 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, darker in front; antennae brownish yellow; mandibles dark brown, slightly paler at the base; labrum light brown; pronotum dingy brown; femora creamy brown, tibiae paler; mesonotal and metanotal plates and abdominal tergites creamy brown and glossy, the first two slightly darker; last abdominal tergite and sternites light brown; sternite 7 slightly paler, the remaining sternites creamy yellow. Head and body sparsely hairy; the last few abdominal tergites and the sternites more densely hairy. Body length 8.40 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular, longer than wide, slightly more than 1.5 times the width; sides nearly straight; posterior margin rounded; frontal face steeply inclined and concave in the middle, bilobed; Y-suture present. Eye spot present, nearly circular, 0.15 mm in diameter, translucent. Ocelli extremely small, white, dot-like. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 ring-like and the shortest; from segment 4 onwards progressively longer, widening and becoming pear-shaped; last segment narrow, oval. Clypeus nearly trapezoidal, indistinctly demarcated from the frontal face, divided into anteclypeus and postclypeus. Postclypeus the same colour as the frontal face, with a few hairs; anteclypeus light brown, paler than the postclypeus, hairless. Labrum nearly square, with long hairs near the apex and a few other short hairs on the body. Mandibles short, thick and stout, weakly incurved at the tip; with a few fine hairs at the base; outer margin weakly incurved behind the middle. Left mandible with 3 marginal teeth, right mandible with 2. Postmentum long, club-shaped, with a narrow and long waist; the sides slightly incurved before the widest point; the minimum width less than half of the maximum width; constriction index 0.42. Pronotum nearly rectangular, slightly narrower than the head, slightly more than half as long as wide; anterior margin broadly incurved, without a notch; posterior margin weakly concave in the middle. Mesonotum and metanotum with small lateral projections. Legs short and thick; apical tibial spurs 3:3:3; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen long, nearly cylindrical, slightly narrowed near the apex; cerci 2-segmented, hairy, 0.15 mm long; styli short, one-segmented, 0.1 mm long, finger-like. Measurements: body length about 8.40 mm; head with mandibles 3.20 mm; head to the mandible base 2.25 mm; maximum head width 1.48 mm; head height 1.23 mm; head index 0.657; diameter of the eye spot 0.15 mm; length of the left and right mandibles each 1.00 mm; labrum 0.33 mm long and 0.38 mm wide; postmentum 1.78 mm long, maximum width 0.55 mm, waist width 0.23 mm, constriction index 0.42; pronotum 0.83 mm long, maximum width 1.40 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original work gives this caste as a Pseudo-worker. Head creamy yellow, slightly paler in front; antennae and legs creamy white; pronotum and abdomen slightly paler than the head. Head and body rather densely hairy. Body length 6.3—7.5 mm. Head nearly circular, slightly wider than the length to the mandible base (length to the tip of the labrum 1.45—1.60 mm, length to the mandible base 1.2—1.30 mm, maximum width 1.25—1.40 mm); Y-suture absent. Eyes small, nearly oval, their long diameter distinctly smaller than the head width.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type material: 1 soldier and several pseudo-workers, collected on 16 September 1988 (month 9) by T. K. Pal and his collecting team near Lichi, Lower Subansari Dist., Arunachal Pradesh, India, 23 km from Yazali. The species name honours the collector Dr Tarun K. Pal.
